conflicts.description: The same manual's DC Sense/Playfield Power Interlock endpoint cells disagree: folio16 C16 prints CN7 input4 GRY RED and common1 BLK; folio21 C16 prints CN7 input4 GRY and common5 GRY RED. Endpoint wiring is withheld. Public116/startup closed semantics are settled by exact source and do not settle hardware endpoints. Resolution path: A machine owner or factory service technician can compare the actual CN7 harness against the two printed regions.
conflicts.rationale: Both readings preserve the established device functions, public addresses and fitment; only printed connector/wire or address labels differ. Literal readings are retained without treating this as a recreation-level uncertainty.

conflicts.description: Factory folio16 reference87 SIXTH COIN is1-SW-21 and reference89 SLAM TILT is1-SW-22. Exact ROM instead maps node1/position21 to public89 SLAM TILT and node1/position22 to public80 SIXTH COIN. Public routes/names follow the exact source/ROM; physical circuit associations/endpoints are withheld until cabinet-node wiring or direct title inspection resolves this semantic mismatch. Unmapped public87 must not be used as an extra ROM input. Resolution path: A machine owner can trace the cabinet Slam Tilt and Sixth Coin contacts to Node1 connector positions21/22, or supply the exact factory cabinet wiring sheet.

Factory reference43 at8-SW-12 is LEFT RAMP EXIT; the exact ROM's same node8/position12/public43 is RIGHT RAMP. Endpoint routing agrees, but the recreation-facing ramp/path identity requires a title-correct location/ball-path drawing or known-working exact table. Both names are retained. Resolution path: A machine owner can identify the Node8 position12 ramp-exit switch in an exact LE ball-path drawing or labeled physical playfield photo.
